Google (aka Alphabet) Is About to Surpass Apple as the Most Valuable Company In the Galaxy

It's quite silly to claim a company's market cap is their value. Even more so for a company like Google. Their stock distribution was designed such that the stock regularly traded on the market is nonvoting stock enabling the owners to maintain control of the company without having to bend to the whims of share holders. Google also does not pay dividends.

So when you buy stock in Google all you're getting is allocated one imaginary unit of well... nothing really, but one of a limited number of nothings! The value assigned to the company through this method has no direct connection to reality and is instead based exclusively on perception. Of course the same is true of the entire stock market, but at least for other companies the share does at least entail a real voting power. Basically my point here is that to say the value of a company is decided by numberOfImaginarySharesThatDoNothing * imaginaryPriceBasedOnNothingButPerception is just a bizarre method of measuring the 'real' value of a company.

There are even more issues here as well. For instance a market cap is not monetizable. If a majority holder started liquidating any meaningful number of his shares the price would plummet. There's also the recent 'quantitative easing' and other attempts to increase inflation that we recently went through following the recession - these pumped trillions of dollars into the economy further inflating market prices out of touch with reality. Company's market cap is no longer even loosely related to their earnings for instance.
